reason: The muscle messengers meet receivers on the cells and are linked to activating muscle genes, so I'll start that path.
expectation: The messengers will help some cells use their muscle-protein instructions.

alternatives.reason: The supporting-cell path also matches a goal, but either group seems like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The muscle messengers led cells to copy muscle-protein instructions into RNA; the proteins still need to be made.
reaction: The picture makes the difference between the RNA instructions and the unfinished proteins clear.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, so they should help the cells make the pulling proteins from their RNA instructions.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to build muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the supporting-cell path instead.

effect: The cells now have pulling proteins that can slide to shorten them; the support-protein goal remains.
reaction: The sliding-fibre picture helps explain what the proteins do.
reason: The supporting-cell messengers are linked to activating support-protein genes, so they fit the remaining goal.
expectation: Some cells will copy support-protein instructions into RNA.

effect: The supporting-cell messengers led to RNA copies of support-protein instructions; the fibres have not been built yet.
reaction: The parallel with the muscle cells makes the next step clearer.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and they worked with the muscle-protein RNA cells.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to make supporting fibres around them.

effect: The cells made supporting fibres around themselves, completing the chapter and showing a contrast with muscle cells keeping pulling proteins inside.
reaction: The contrast helped make the different cell jobs understandable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the two kinds of protein was worthwhile because the pictures showed how cells with the same DNA can do different jobs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Repeating the messenger-then-amino-acid pattern for supporting cells was somewhat predictable, though it made the comparison clear.

surprise.text: I noticed that muscle cells keep pulling proteins inside, while supporting cells release proteins to build fibres around themselves.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the messenger pictures and the protein-building-block label gave a reason for each pairing.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because I am curious how the separate muscle cells get assembled into larger fibres.
